html:
Moïse Tshombe was the leader of the State of Katanga, which broke away from the newly independent Congo on 11 July 1960, and later prime minister of the whole country.

A businessman from a leading Lunda family, he was backed by Belgian officers, white mercenaries and the mining company Union Minière. Lumumba was handed over to his forces in January 1961 and killed.

United Nations troops ended the secession in January 1963 and he went into exile, but returned as prime minister in 1964 to fight the Simba rebellion with mercenaries. Mobutu removed him, and he died in custody in Algeria in 1969, after the Congo Crisis.
